environment.browserNameAndVersion: Google Chrome 151.0.7922.138 via Playwright MCP fallback
environment.networkCondition: Online baseline plus Playwright context offline reload; a remote probe failed with net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED while the local deck remained usable.
environment.themeCondition: Light and dark modes exercised; the dark override persisted across reload and the deck returned to light after the test.
environment.reducedMotionCondition: No-preference baseline plus prefers-reduced-motion: reduce emulation; representative transition and animation durations were 0.01ms with zero running animations.
environment.colorModeCondition: Light and dark color schemes plus text-and-shape Ready, Watch, and Stop cues.
environment.notes: The connected browser was unavailable, so the operator-authorized Playwright MCP fallback executed the manual UAT at 360 and 1280 CSS px. The driver remains manual because no repository harness was committed.

rows.claim: The slide-deck reader opens directly over file:// with its expected title and no server dependency or visible error state.
rows.observedResult: Opened the exact repository-relative template over file://. The document title was Slide Deck - RACE-421 Release Confidence, the visible h1 was RACE-421 Release Confidence, the page rendered without a server, and the final online load reported zero console errors.

rows.claim: The deck-title, slides, and speaker-notes fills contain complete representative reader content.
rows.observedResult: The release-review kicker, title, audience/date/presenter subtitle, all three anchored articles (#slides-readiness-map, #slides-evidence-lane, and #slides-release-call), Talk track heading, and three ordered speaker notes were present. The notes matched the visible slide order.

rows.claim: The deck exposes a named navigation group, named previous/next controls, and a polite current-position region.
rows.observedResult: The accessibility snapshot exposed navigation named Slide deck navigation, buttons named Previous slide and Next slide, aria-controls=deck-stage on both buttons, and #slide-count as an aria-live=polite position message.

rows.claim: Previous/next controls, all declared keyboard keys, and a bounded wheel gesture move through the three-slide set.
rows.observedResult: Next moved 1 to 2 and Previous moved 3 to 2. ArrowRight, ArrowDown, and PageDown moved forward; ArrowLeft, ArrowUp, and PageUp moved backward; End and Home selected the last and first slides. Trusted Playwright wheel input moved one slide, an immediate repeat was locked at the same slide, and a later reverse gesture moved one slide back.

rows.claim: Only the active slide remains visible and interactive; inactive slides are removed from keyboard and accessibility traversal.
rows.observedResult: At every position, the active article had hidden=false, inert=false, and aria-hidden=false. Both inactive articles had hidden=true, inert=true, and aria-hidden=true. Accessibility snapshots exposed only the active article, and Tab traversal never entered inactive slide content.

rows.claim: The deck never advances automatically while idle or while the deck stage is focused.
rows.observedResult: The first observation remained at Slide 1 of 3 for 33.5 seconds with BODY focus unchanged. A second 33.8-second observation remained at Slide 1 of 3 with #deck-stage focused; the stage's temporary runtime tabindex used only for this observation was removed afterward.

rows.claim: The local reader remains usable after an offline reload.
rows.observedResult: Playwright context offline mode produced net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED for a remote navigation probe. In the same offline context, the file:// deck reloaded with its expected title, heading, theme control, three notes, and navigation; Next advanced to Slide 2 of 3. Network mode was restored after the observation.

rows.claim: Forward and backward keyboard traversal reaches every enabled control in deterministic order at each navigation boundary.
rows.observedResult: At slide 1 the forward order was .rc-theme-toggle then #next-slide and Shift+Tab returned to the theme control. At slide 2, from the focused article, Tab reached #previous-slide then #next-slide and Shift+Tab returned to #previous-slide. At slide 3, from the focused article, Tab reached #previous-slide while disabled #next-slide and all inactive slide content were skipped.

rows.claim: Light and dark themes preserve the same deck content, controls, focus, and slide state.
rows.observedResult: Light rendered rgb(247, 246, 244) background with rgb(17, 24, 39) text; dark rendered rgb(26, 26, 26) with rgb(230, 230, 230) text. The title, three slide headings, three notes, counter, control availability, and hidden/inert states were identical. Dark persisted across reload, and keyboard focus remained visible.

rows.claim: Reduced-motion mode preserves complete slide behavior without requiring animation to understand state.
rows.observedResult: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched, representative element and pseudo-element transition/animation durations computed to 1e-05s (0.01ms), document.getAnimations() reported zero running animations, and keyboard navigation still moved from slides 1 to 2 to 3 with matching focus and position text.

rows.claim: Ready, Watch, and Stop meaning remains understandable without relying on hue.
rows.observedResult: Slide 3 exposed the visible labels Status: Ready, Status: Watch, and Status: Stop. Its legend repeated Ready - circle, Watch - square, and Stop - block; computed pseudo-element border radii were 999px, 2px, and 0px respectively.

rows.claim: The reader follows the no-horizontal-scroll-region route when source and runtime expose no meaningful horizontal scroll element.
rows.observedResult: Source inspection found no overflow-x:auto or overflow-x:scroll and only html/body overflow-x:hidden. At 360 CSS px, document clientWidth and scrollWidth were both 345; at 1280 CSS px both were 1265. All three slides reported no element with horizontal content overflow and no actual user-scroll region.

rows.claim: All three slides remain complete and usable at exactly 360 CSS px without horizontal overflow, clipping, or overlap.
rows.observedResult: At viewport 360x800, document and body clientWidth equaled scrollWidth at 345 CSS px on all three slides. No visible element extended beyond the viewport, no hidden/clip overflow concealed content, navigation items did not intersect, fixed-theme text-ink overlap was empty, and full-page screenshots showed complete slide, note, legend, and control content.

rows.claim: All three slides remain complete and usable at a desktop width of at least 1280 CSS px without horizontal overflow, clipping, or overlap.
rows.observedResult: At viewport 1280x900, document and body clientWidth equaled scrollWidth at 1265 CSS px on all three slides. No visible element extended beyond the viewport, no hidden/clip overflow concealed content, navigation items did not intersect, the fixed theme control overlapped no rendered text ink, and full-page screenshots showed complete content.

rows.claim: The slide-deck manifest entry matches the exhaustive ART-005 ID, title, source, role, status, and export classification.
